sample_unit: regimen-specific monthly national ART consumption time series

links.outcome: Signed percentage deviation of foundation/hybrid models versus classical baselines across ART regimens
links.effect: No single model best across regimens. Hybrid 70th percentile SPD -2.02% for adult AZT+3TC vs other models' range [-15.7, 8.87]; Holt-Winters best for adult RTV booster (1.68% vs 14.94-17.25%).
links.quote: Performance varied across regimens, indicating that no single approach was best-performing for all formulations.

links.outcome: Systematic directional forecast error across pediatric regimens for all models
links.effect: All models over-predicted pediatric ABC+3TC (SPD -82.74 to -67.43) and under-predicted pediatric AZT+3TC (24.93 to 63.73) and LPV/r 100/25 (18.32 to 52.07).
links.quote: For pediatric ABC+3TC, all models over-predicted within a narrow band of [−82.74, −67.43], while for pediatric AZT+3TC and LPV/r 100/25, all models under-predicted, with ranges of [24.93, 63.73] and [18.32, 52.07], respectively.

unlisted_practices: Regimen-specific model selection for demand forecasting
Regimen-specific model-error buffer applied to under-prediction for procurement planning
No-code dashboard deployment of forecasting workflow
Synthetic privacy-preserving dataset for pipeline development

screen.reason: Evaluates time-series foundation models (TimesFM) and classical models for HIV drug demand forecasting, and tests an operational safeguard/practice (regimen-specific model-error buffering and directional error reporting) to translate forecasts into procurement recommendations.
